title: Prove exact contiguous helper storage: 5q versus peak 4q (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove an exact storage obstruction for eight fixed half-open helper lifetimes. For every positive real scale q:

```text
peak live width                 4q
minimum with split fixed sets   4q
minimum with contiguous blocks  5q
```

Claim type: scoped mathematical proof with finite corroboration. The explicit family forces a 25% storage surcharge even when all lifetimes are known in advance. A real-to-integer compression lemma and a four-cell contradiction prove the lower bound; displayed layouts attain both optima.

This takes the contiguous-block boundary explicitly excluded by Ali Romman's PR #5763 at `cee2336bc3a20c586b1dbb55152d97a114c657a6`. The predecessor is cited as the question source and split-range context, not audited or replayed. Classical dynamic storage allocation is credited; novelty of the general fragmentation phenomenon is not claimed. This result was produced by Nick Petalas.

## Evidence

- Before: peak live width alone provides no contiguous layout certificate under the changed contract.
- After: the explicit family has exact optima 4q and 5q. The verifier checks all 40,320 total address orders, independently excludes all 9,216 capacity-four integer placements, validates both layouts at six exact rational scales, and rejects four invalid layouts.
- CPython 3.12.15 warning-strict normal and optimized runs pass with `PASS_CONTIGUOUS_HELPER_STORAGE_GAP`, timed locally at 0.52s and 0.53s. Both registered VERIFY commands and package metadata checks pass.
- Committed bytes and declared source history pass at `d46194d7f001210e49ef155409b76182c773e6e7`. A generated local receipt binds all five package hashes. Read-only review found no mathematical error in the new proof or layouts.

From the checkout root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/contiguous-helper-storage-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/contiguous-helper-storage-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/contiguous-helper-storage-gap
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/contiguous-helper-storage-gap --check-source-history
```

Elsewhere, substitute a CPython 3.12 interpreter for the absolute interpreter path. Standard library only.

## Limitations

The proof fixes lifetimes, widths and addresses throughout each lifetime. It does not permit movement, change chronology, prove a smallest obstruction, or establish a worst-case approximation ratio. The all-positive-real statement has a written proof; finite enumeration corroborates its unit instance.

No actual supplier is asserted to require contiguous blocks. Source-specific cleanup, routing, ownership, precision, tape movement and all-size compiler obligations are unrun and outside this claim. No native construction, new kappa, selected-frontier change or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Related open work

- #5763 supplies the split-range allocator and explicitly excludes contiguity. This contribution proves an exact obstruction for that changed interface, without testing its predecessor implementation.
- #5822 allocates actual P104 private lifetimes into unit slots. The present family has unequal widths and does not recompute or challenge its source-specific slot count.
- #5893 charges migration across two eligible reusable resources. The present contract fixes addresses during each lifetime and prices capacity instead of transfers.
- #5780 and #5895 optimize reversible scratch with recomputation and chronology choices. The present obstruction uses supplied immutable lifetimes.
- #5886 renames bounded NTT temporaries into reusable cells. The present family is a storage-contract example and does not change that program or its claimed count.
- #5880 proves clean information storage for reversible Gaussian overwrite. That information-theoretic contract is separate from fixed weighted lifetime placement.
- #5898 studies one initially clean, restored helper in scalar bank exchange. Its six-ADD gate-count floor does not price contiguous weighted lifetime storage; no common numerical fixture is evaluated here.

- #5905 proves retained payload storage for one-pass child batching. Its streaming-information model permits encoding and has a different fixed input/output order; this result prices fixed contiguous placement of already specified lifetimes. No common numerical instance is computed.

## Open next questions

- Can an actual native caller use split fixed ranges with its complete route and address-description bill? Start with a source-pinned access trace and a declared movement contract.
- Which source-derived lifetime restrictions guarantee contiguous storage at peak width? First identify a restriction that excludes this eight-helper pattern.
